prior_art: none — the #7174 by-eye checks (byeye-pages.json) were 6 lite pages; this is the apply gate on flash pages
method: 20 flash pages per round from the latin-repair-census books, seeded draw (gate-draw seeds 5924023, 7174, 1022, 31415), half habit / half no-habit pages; 4 independent Opus readers per round, zoomed crops of the R2 image (getPageSource); every change checked on pages <= 40 changes, else >= 3 per token type and all risky types

rounds.rule: pass + tags/caps/vernacular cut, attested>=20 & >=2% only on no-habit pages

verdicts.notes: Clean 1629 roman type. Every changed word (fonteſque, univerſa, poſterius, ipſa, occaſu x2, eſt, ipſo, diſtinguitur, clariſſimi) shows a long s with no crossbar to the right of the stem. Proper names (Patiſſus, Boryſthenes, Iſter, Tranſſilvani, Mœſia, Caucaſum, Aſia) also print ſ, but the pass left them as f, so nothing was altered; it under-corrects there.

Low-resolution scan (1266x1984) but the 1529 roman is legible line by line. I read all 13 bands plus the margin notes; every changed letter is ſ in print. Risky cases: L15 margin 'Quòd deus ſit, & quid ſit' is an italic ſ with no bar (right); L12 'fas → ſas' is the second half of 'cau/ſas' split at the line end, not the word fas (right); 'fui → ſui', 'fi → ſi', 'fol → ſol', 'fex → ſex' are all ſ in print. True f's (differt, efficitur, fatuus) were left alone.

1609 roman and italic. All 30 changes confirmed in zoomed crops: italic ſecundum, ſorbili, iuſculo, generoſo, poſſunt; roman ſal, menſtrua, ſolutionem, eſt, magiſterij, obſeruetur, ſpiritum, ſpagyricum, ſuppoſitus, eſſet, ſed, ſubinde, inſtar, ſpumæ, craſſa, deſtilla. In all of them the bar sits only to the left of the stem (ſ).

Print has laceſſit (ſſ ligature), ſeſe, iſtiuſ-, iſtiuſmodi, so each changed letter is ſ. The results are mixed forms (lacesſit, istiuſ): the OCR had already normalised the other long s's to s. That is not an error of the pass.
1600 Ammianus. Crops confirm diſſimulata, inſaniente (italic margin note '...modum in-ſaniente?'), reſtitiſſet, perfuſorum, popoſcerat, intromiſſa, inſidias, obſcuriſſimis. All are ſ in print.

1589 italic verse (Aratea). Every changed letter is a clear italic long s with no right crossbar (paſſis, ſubſequitur, ſpecie, ſtellarum, ſoliti, ſimili, eſt, eſſe, ſerpunt...). Unchanged f's are true f's (fultum, forma, flamen, fulgore). Proper names Cynofura/Caffiepeia were left untouched, though the print has ſ there, so those are misses, not wrong changes.

18th-c. roman/italic Porphyry commentary. Every real-word-risk change was read in the crops and all are ſ: fine→ſine (L30, 'ſine dubio'), fit→ſit (L49, L58), fe→ſe (L37, L42, L63), fed→ſed, fuo→ſuo, folis/folo→ſolis/ſolo. True f's left alone (fendi, feritas, ferventes, infoecundi). Misses, not errors: Refpiciunt, Expreffit and the name Beklenfes stayed unchanged.

Two-page spread, 18th-c. roman type (Zohar preface). I read every changed line on both pages and in the footnotes. All are long s, including the real-word risks fatis→ſatis ×2, fit→ſit, fi→ſi, fe→ſe ×2, fed, fint, fui, fuis, fub, femper, fibi, fqq/fq. Where the print has a round s inside ſſ (generoſisſimus, ſerenisſimus, arcesſiuerint), the letter is still s, never f. True f's are untouched: fuit, ferreis, fatendum, the folio 'f.' in the notes. Proper names (Chrifti, Mofis, Rofenroth, Auguftus, Francifcus, Meffia) were left unchanged.

All 3 (aſſidentem, ſa-[lutem], ceſſerunt) clearly show long s in the print. The page is habit:false: the rest of the OCR uses round s, so the output now mixes ſ and s. The letters are right, but the orthography is inconsistent.

All 4 are læſio-/læſione forms, and the roman long s is clear (nick on the left only). The page is habit:false: the rest of the OCR is normalised to round s (si, est, sine), so the result mixes ſ and s.

Clean 1715 roman with crisp long s. 'ſine vulnere' (L7) shows the left-only nick; 'in fine' (L11) has a true f and was correctly left. Italic 'eſt mirum ſi' is ſ. Missed by the pass, not a wrong change: 'ferventur' (print ſerventur) is still f.

verdicts.notes: Vesalius Fabrica 1555: crisp roman with clear ſ vs f. All body-text changes in L21 and L32 show ſ (incl. ſi x2, ſe, ſed, ſua, ſic, ſecus, and the first ſit "ipſius ſit uſus"). 1529 Basel roman: manſerit x2 and ſubmerſi all clearly long s (no right-side crossbar) in the image.

1701 small-format roman, high contrast: every changed token (perſpir- x9, ſuillæ x2, ſimul, ingeſta, uſu, ſolito, conſuetæ, ſudorem, faceſſere, ſolet, fortaſſè, ſenſibiliter, ſentitur) shows ſ; genuine f (ficus, faceſſere, fortaſſè initial) left untouched.

verdicts.notes: Clean roman type (Ortelius 1578), read at high zoom in 8 bands: every changed letter is a long s with left-only nick, including the proper name luſitaniæ (L12) and abbreviation-free tokens. Many f-for-ſ errors remain unchanged (Lufus, Lufitania, Infignis, Rhodienfium, Cœpiffe, Vlyfsipona), so the pass under-corrects but does no harm.

1518 rotunda, legible: all 50 changes show ſ in print (iſaias, iſrael, meſſiā etc.). Real f kept correctly in fuiſſe; 'fit meffias' and the 'f.' (ſ. = scilicet) were left unchanged though the print shows ſ.

Same 1518 rotunda; all 9 show ſ in print. In feciſti only the inner f was changed (initial f of fecisti correctly kept); L13 ſerue (servant) is ſ in print, not ferue.
Aldine italic (1534 Valerius Maximus); nobiliſſimi, præſto, promptiſſimus all clearly long-s ligatures in print.

Roman text in Prop. V and the italic enunciation of Prop. VI both print long s at every changed spot (ſequenti, propoſitionem, neceſſe, eſt, conſideretur, ſuperficies, dimenſio, conſequens; ſub, exiſtentes, ſunt, baſin). The pass missed one: 'fit' in L11 is ſit in the print and was left as f.

Clean roman Latin (Julian, Misopogon); every changed letter is a long s (or ſſ ligature) in the print. Real f's nearby (feliciores, afficitis, faciendi, facultate, fruimini) were correctly left alone.

French-catalogued book, but this page is an italic Latin quotation (Philalethes), so every changed token is Latin. All 15 show italic ſ; real f in fuit, profiteor and fratrem was left unchanged. The pass missed 'Cofmopolitam' (the print has Coſmopolitam).
Dark italic print, but legible at zoom: iuſ-(sit), religaſ-(se), reuiuiſcere all show italic long s.
'aſſidué' is a roman ſſ ligature, and the italic marginal note reads 'quaſ-dā' with long s. Both changes are right.

Clean 1522 roman print; every changed word read in zoomed strips over both columns. Every changed f is a long s (left-only nick), including seruit, sane, si, se, semp (abbrev.), ideſt. Real f in the print (fili, feliciter, fruit, formam, factus) was not touched.

Bitonal 1497 Aldine scan, still legible at zoom. Every changed token reads long s, including the risky 'fui' (= sen-|ſui, dative of sensus), si, sic, se, sed, sane. True f words (facit, familiaria, fit, fiue, profecto) were correctly left alone.

meaning_changes.why: Print has a true f with a crossbar through the stem: 'infectatur' (is infected by marsh exhalation). The change makes 'insectatur' (pursues), a different real word.
Print has the fl ligature, f crossbar visible: 'Choro flante' (when the north-west wind blows). 'slante' is not a word, and the verb is lost.

flāte (fl ligature with a true f)

verdicts.notes: The habit check reads f:0 s:28 for this page (the OCR already gave ſ correctly), yet the pass still ran. Both f-words it changed were real f. Only inſertas is right (print shows ſ).
All four are ſſ ligatures in the 1624 roman (tetigiſſe, descendiſſe, fortaſſis, deflexiſſe). The OCR had read them as ff. All right.
Fludd 1617: ſunt (diagram), ſimilitudinibus, ſimilitudine and luminoſo all show long s in the print. All right.

Cluverius 1624, roman text plus italic Livy quotations. Every changed word shows a clear long s (no right-hand crossbar) in the image, including fi->ſi, fe->ſe, fint->ſint, funt->ſunt, faltu/faltus/faltum, fuiffe->fuiſſe. The Italian 'Rocca di monte Dragone' was not touched. Many f-for-ſ errors were left unchanged (fatis, Sinueffa, Teanenfes, Vefcinum, Maffici, Hierofolymitano, fit), so the page is still in mixed orthography after the pass.

Muretus's notes on Terence (1560), large clean italic. Every changed word has a long s in print, including the two sed->ſed and si->ſi. In conuiuifque the print abbreviates as 'cõuiuijsq.' with a short round s, so the letter is s and the change counts as right. Missed by the pass: fine (ſine), confideret, Sponfalia, Craffipedi.
Aldine Iamblichus (1497), binarized roman image. ſeruant (x2), cõſeruant, emphaſim and inſinuationis all have a long s in print. The real f in 'feruntur' on the same lines was correctly left alone.

Pimander (1522), two-page spread in roman. vniuerſi, vniuerſa and vniuerſis all have a long s in print. The rest of the OCR already writes every long s as round s (habit false), so these three ſ are now inconsistent with the rest of the page, though the letter itself is correct.

Terence, Phormio V.6 (1560), italic verse. oneraſtis, exoneraſtis and ceſſo all have a long s (ſt ligature and ſſ) in print. The rest of the OCR writes round s (habit false), so the page now mixes ſ and s, though the letters are correct.

verdicts.notes: Clean italic 1607 print with long s throughout (Cognoſce, ſub, ſunt, eſt, ſummus, aſſiduum ligature, eſſe); every changed token shows ſ in the image. The pass left some f-for-ſ errors in place (Cognofce, efse, Eft, Ipfe, proficifcitur, fit), but no wrong edits.

1767 roman print with long s everywhere; all 47 changes (deteſtabitur, maſculi, ſexus, ſemen, ſcholion, fuiſſe, coepiſſe etc.) match the image. Greek lemmata and the proper name Weſſeling were left untouched. Some errors remain unfixed (fit, fol, Nofter, Eufeb), and 'fimum' is correctly left as f.

1593 two-column roman print with ſ used throughout. 'infuiſitas' (print: inſulſitas) and 'inſtit' (print: inſit) are earlier OCR misreads; in both, the letter the pass changed is ſ in the print.
Small roman prayer-book page. 'dulciſſi' shows the ſſ ligature and 'croſanctum' a clear ſ. 'Amabiliffime' on the same line was not converted (print has ſſ).

The OCR is mostly normalised to round s already; the 5 changes fix leftovers, and the image shows ſ in each (ſigno, permoleſtum, eſcas, ꝑſoluti, deterſis). Remaining leftovers such as 'facculum' and 'effer' were not touched.

verdicts.notes: 1489 roman incunable printed with ſ throughout. Every other change matches a printed ſ (ſint, ſunt, ſcalpit, noſtris, forſitan, ſup, etc.); the only error is the f of the hyphenated 'festiue' at the end of L10.

1529 roman/italic page, ſ used in every non-final position, including the margin note 'Quòd ſalus noſtra ex deo eſt'. I read the whole page in zoomed bands. Every changed token shows ſ; true initial f's (feciſti, feſtina, faſtidiuit, ferienti) were correctly kept.

1609 roman print with ſ throughout; all 32 changed tokens show ſ in the image. Not part of the verdict: L12 'falem', 'fulphure' and 'Eft' were left unchanged, but the print has ſalem, ſulphure, Eſt, so they are misses, not errors.

All three show printed ſ (ſępe at L34, ſæpe at L48, inſi-|gnem at L49), so each letter is right. This page's OCR otherwise writes round s, so these three ſ are inconsistent with the rest of the page (habit=false). 'infixus' was correctly left alone.

Vesalius 1555 roman: 'commiſſum' and 'tãtiſper' clearly show ſſ / ſ, so both are right. The rest of the OCR normalizes to round s (habit=false), so the two ſ are typographically inconsistent with the page.

Clean, high-resolution 1501 roman type. Every changed spot shows a long s with no right-hand crossbar (epiſtola, proſpere, noſtræ, poſſidetis, ſubii, ſua, eſt, ſacrilegiiq, uetuſtos, religioſiſſimis, co̅ſpexerint, poſtlimi, chriſtiana, geſta, noſtraciis, etc.); true f (fines, fundatis, fœlicitate) has a crossbar on both sides.

The image is only 600px wide, so the letters are blurry, but the body-text long s is still clearly different from f (futuro, feritas, facis, formidine have full crossbars). Two cannot_tell: L8 margin 'poft→poſt' (tiny italic marginal note) and L9 'humilibúfque→humilibúſque' (smudged). All f-forms were non-words, and in context all are certainly s.

1486 Lucretius roman type, clear. uiciſſim, ſceleris, ſcelerosa and both ſimul show long s. Untouched 'in fula' on L31 also reads 'in ſula' (infula) in print, which is a remaining OCR error but not one of these changes.

1486 roman incunable (Lucretius). Every changed letter is clearly long s in the print: there is no right-hand crossbar, unlike f in forent/finem/refici. parafset → paraſset is right at the changed letter, but the print has paraſſet, so the second s is still a pre-existing OCR error. Unchanged poffint (L12, L28) and Diffolui, Effe are also ſ in print but were left alone.
